# D8_TRIGDEBUG_L7cc56d99: per-bar values of trig_levels_vwap break (n 2, k 0.25) on the _CANC lbrk_3_40 bars, td 20261110, NY AM session plus the 300 bars before it; 1-minute series and anchor state (W-D8SPEC, relay order 1930Z)

Series: ONE continuous series of all bars of the row on `_CANC` bars (`/mnt/l2/l2vast/_d8spec/bars_c/lbrk_3_40`, 69,766 bars). Rows: bar index 69194 to 69526 (idx = row number); NY AM bars of 20261110 = sess 3 and td 20261110 (idx 69494 to 69526, 33 bars; 10 events in that session). I recomputed every column with the engine's own helpers (`fd_common.decision_s`, `lines_at_idx`, `level_events`) and checked the signals over the whole series equal the module's `signal_fn` (15930 signals; equal = True).

## Exact definitions (code: `th_grid/trig_levels_vwap.py` -> `triggers_d/lv_vwap.py`, `lv_base.py`, `fd_common.py`, `fd_levels.py`)
- **T0 (decision time)** of bar j = floor to whole seconds of the KNOWN time of bar j-1 (`t_close[j-1] // 10**9`); the bar series has no open time so t_open is not used; bar 0 of the series has no T0. Column T0 below.
- **Level lookup:** the lines live on a 1-minute grid (minute START times, epoch s); for bar j take the last minute whose start <= T0 (searchsorted right minus 1); the value is valid only if T0 - minute_start <= 120 s (else NaN); the value stored at minute i uses minutes BEFORE i only (the VWAP through the end of minute i-1). So the line used for a bar is the VWAP through the last COMPLETED minute before T0's minute (T0 inside minute m uses minutes < m).
- **The eight lines** (RAW price domain: lines are built on back-adjusted prices, raw = adjusted - off[i]; off = 0 on 2026-11-10): VWAP0 = VWAP of typical price (h+l+c)/3 x volume from the start of the trading day (18:00 ET minute) valid when minutes-since-18:00 >= 30 and cumulative volume > 2000; RVWAP0 = same anchored at 09:30 ET, valid 09:45-16:00 ET and cum vol > 2000; LVWAP0 = anchored 02:00 ET, valid 02:15-16:00 ET and cum vol > 1000; YVWAP = prior trading date's RTH (09:30-16:00 ET) sum(typ*v)/sum(v), constant for the whole next trading date; AVPDH / AVPDL = VWAP anchored at the minute of the prior RTH day's HIGH / LOW (first max h / min l of RTH minutes), running from that minute through the last completed minute, used for the whole next trading date; WVWAP = anchored at the first minute of the ISO week of the TRADING DATE (trading date = ET + 6 h, so the week starts Sunday 18:00 ET), valid when cumulative volume > 20000; MVWAP = anchored at the first minute of the calendar month of the trading date, valid when cumulative volume > 20000. All are plain cumulative sums of typ*v and v (typ = (high+low+close)/3 of each 1-minute bar, v = contracts); NaN where not valid.
- **u** = 5.0 points fixed (the variant is `break`, not `break_native`), so k*u = 1.25 points. **Event (n 2, k 0.25)** per line: long when the close of bar j AND the close of bar j-1 are both > level(bar j's T0) + 1.25 and the close of bar j-2 was <= level + 1.25 (the SAME level value, taken at bar j's T0, is used for all three comparisons), short mirrored; edge-triggered; a bar that gives both a long on one line and a short on another is dropped. **line fired** = the first line in the order above that has an event on that bar (its level is shown); long/short flags are over all lines. Event time = floor(known time) + 2 s.

## History NT8 must load (plain paragraph)
VWAP0, RVWAP0 and LVWAP0 only need the current trading day from 18:00 ET (and are NaN for the first 30 / 15 / 15 minutes after their anchors or until the volume gate). YVWAP needs the whole RTH session of the PREVIOUS trading date (the previous date present in the data: Friday for a Monday, and after a holiday the last open day), and AVPDH / AVPDL need the previous trading date's RTH minutes to find its high and low minute plus every minute from that extreme until now, so up to about 1.5 trading days (about 3.5 calendar days over a weekend). WVWAP runs from Sunday 18:00 ET of the current trading week (up to about 5 trading days, 6 calendar days, of minutes). MVWAP is the one that matters: it runs from the FIRST minute of the calendar month of the trading date (up to about 23 trading days, 31 calendar days of 1-minute data, about 32,000 minutes), so NT8 must load at least one calendar month of 1-minute data (35 calendar days to be safe) before a MVWAP line equals the engine's; on day one of a month the previous month's data are needed only for YVWAP/AVPDH/AVPDL. The weekly and monthly sums cross contract rolls only in the weeks/months that contain a roll (quarterly, mid March/June/September/December): then the older minutes must be back-adjusted by the roll step before summing (the engine lifts older contracts onto the newest); in November 2026 there is no roll, so raw = adjusted. **Engine artefact to know about:** the engine's 1-minute data for November 2026 has a tape hole: the first minute of the month in the data is 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC (trading dates 11-02 to 11-04 and the morning of 11-05 are missing), so the engine's MVWAP in November is anchored at 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC (cum volume 2,202,461 contracts carried into 11-10, VWAP 27,277.95), NOT at the true first minute of the month; a correct NT8 MVWAP will therefore differ from the engine's for the whole of November (and WVWAP/AVPDH/AVPDL/YVWAP do not have this problem on 11-10). Any engine event whose fired line is MVWAP in November is not reproducible by a complete-month NT8 build. The lines also require that the 1-minute bars be built from trades exactly like the engine's (typical price of each trade-minute: high/low/close over all prints of the minute, volume = sum of contract sizes, minute = floor of the print's UTC time to the minute, no empty minutes) and that the trading-date/week/month keys use ET + 6 hours. Nothing else (no order book, no other instrument) is used.
